entities.name: Philip IV of Macedon
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Philip IV of Macedon was a brief king of the ancient Greek kingdom of Macedonia in 297 BC, belonging to the Antipatrid dynasty.

 As the son of Thessalonike, daughter of Philip II, and Cassander, king of Macedonia, Philip IV played a pivotal role in shaping the course of Macedonian history.

 His reign was marked by power struggles and internal conflicts, ultimately leading to his downfall and the rise of the Seleucid Empire.

 The legacy of Philip IV continues to be felt in the modern era, with the city of Thessaloniki still bearing his name.

 'The Macedonians are a people not easily vanquished, for they are descended from the gods.' - Arrian
